fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: Seals at almost no closing force
A trim clip cannot generate the clamp a solid gasket needs. Closed-cell foam seals at a fraction of it — which is the whole reason this part is foam and not rubber.
Open-cell sponge wicks water straight through the joint it is meant to seal. On a pillar that drains into the body cavity, that is the difference between a seal and a leak path.
Foam is bought on density, compression force deflection and ASTM D1056 grade. Send the gap range and the closing force and we will specify the rest.
Moulded to shape for a complex section, or die-cut from sponge sheet for a flat profile — with self-adhesive backing applied if you want it fitted in one action on the line.
fields.note:
Four cards, four cards — no count change and no new element.
Card 01 is the product argument and the live page does not make it anywhere. Foam versus solid is a closing-force decision, and a body engineer specifying against a clip-fixed trim panel knows it immediately.
Card 02 is the one that prevents a warranty claim. Open-cell sponge in a wet pillar joint is a classic water-ingress cause, and naming the distinction is the fastest way to sound like a supplier who has made this part.
Card 04 carries the ISO scope consequence quietly — moulded or die-cut is also the answer to whether the certificate covers it

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: Step 03 is the wrong process for this part
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · step 03 says “Compression Moulding”; a foam seal is blown and die-cut

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The blowing agent and its loading are set here, and they are what fix the density.
Tool or die design — moulds for a shaped seal, cutting dies for a flat one, made in-house and held as a controlled record.
Expansion and cure — the compound is blown to the specified density and cured, then moulded to shape or calendered to sheet.
Die-cutting or trimming — flat seals die-cut to profile from sheet; moulded seals flash-trimmed. Self-adhesive backing laminated at this stage if specified.
Quality inspection — density, compression force deflection and dimensional check before release.

Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used. Foam is packed uncompressed; sponge stored under load takes a set that does not recover.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept — but four need the foam vocabulary. This is the second-clearest case in the catalogue of the shared component describing the wrong process, after the glazing profile on SKU 02.
Step 01 is the one worth expanding. Density is set by the blowing agent at compounding, not by anything downstream — so a supplier who mixes its own compound controls the density directly. That is a real argument and it belongs to a moulder who compounds in-house, which is exactly what Margo is

notes: The process block must render from the part record. Moulded, extruded, die-cut and blown are four different processes and the template names one.
“Blowing agent”, “closed-cell” and “die-cut” are foam-buyer vocabulary and none appears on this site.
Numbered steps are an <ol>.
